root_cause.text: The vsock_update_buffer_size() function was performing constraint checks in the wrong order, allowing the minimum buffer size check to override the maximum buffer size check when minimum was configured larger than maximum, thereby violating the intended upper bound constraint.
root_cause.evidence: The patch reorders the clamping logic in vsock_update_buffer_size() by moving the minimum check before the maximum check. The original code clamped to maximum first (line removed: `if (val > vsk->buffer_max_size) val = vsk->buffer_max_size;`), then to minimum, which meant if buffer_min_size > buffer_max_size, the final minimum clamp would override the maximum clamp. The fix ensures the maximum clamp executes last, guaranteeing vsk->buffer_size never exceeds vsk->buffer_max_size regardless of the minimum value configuration.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vsock_update_buffer_size() function introduced in this commit contains the vulnerable construct. The function performs constraint checks in the wrong order: it first checks if val > vsk->buffer_max_size (line 8-9), then checks if val < vsk->buffer_min_size (line 11-12). This ordering is problematic because if buffer_min_size is configured larger than buffer_max_size, the minimum check will override the maximum check. For example, if buffer_max_size=100 and buffer_min_size=200, a requested val=150 would first pass the max check (150 is not > 100, so no change), but then fail the min check (150 < 200 is false, so no change), resulting in val=150 which violates the maximum constraint. The correct fix would require checking the relationship between min and max first, or reordering the checks so the maximum constraint is enforced after the minimum constraint. The code as shown does not contain this fix.
